articles.title: Outlook Not Opening
steps: Close Outlook completely from Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc)
Press Win + R → type outlook.exe /safe → press Enter
If opens in safe mode → disable add-ins → File → Options → Add-ins → Manage COM Add-ins → uncheck all → restart
articles.text: Email & Outlook Outlook Not Opening Close Outlook completely from Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc) Press Win + R → type outlook.exe /safe → press Enter If opens in safe mode → disable add-ins → File → Options → Add-ins → Manage COM Add-ins → uncheck all → restart

articles.title: Outlook Not Syncing / Emails Not Receiving
steps: Check internet connection first
Click Send/Receive → Send/Receive All Folders
Check if Outlook is set to Work Offline → View tab → uncheck Work Offline
Remove and re-add account → File → Account Settings → select account → Remove → Add again
articles.text: Email & Outlook Outlook Not Syncing / Emails Not Receiving Check internet connection first Click Send/Receive → Send/Receive All Folders Check if Outlook is set to Work Offline → View tab → uncheck Work Offline Remove and re-add account → File → Account Settings → select account → Remove → Add again

articles.title: Emails Stuck in Outbox
steps: Check attachment size — Nomura limit is 25MB
Delete the stuck email from Outbox folder
Restart Outlook and retry with a smaller attachment
articles.text: Email & Outlook Emails Stuck in Outbox Check attachment size — Nomura limit is 25MB Delete the stuck email from Outbox folder Restart Outlook and retry with a smaller attachment

articles.title: Outlook Password Keeps Asking
steps: Go to Control Panel → Credential Manager → Windows Credentials
Find Microsoft Office entries → Remove them
Restart Outlook → sign in fresh with Nomura credentials
articles.text: Email & Outlook Outlook Password Keeps Asking Go to Control Panel → Credential Manager → Windows Credentials Find Microsoft Office entries → Remove them Restart Outlook → sign in fresh with Nomura credentials

articles.title: Emails Going to Junk / Spam
steps: Check Junk Email folder
Right click email → Mark as Not Junk
Add sender to Safe Senders → Home → Junk → Junk Email Options → Safe Senders → Add
articles.text: Email & Outlook Emails Going to Junk / Spam Check Junk Email folder Right click email → Mark as Not Junk Add sender to Safe Senders → Home → Junk → Junk Email Options → Safe Senders → Add

articles.title: Teams Not Loading / Stuck on Loading Screen
steps: Close Teams completely from Task Manager
Press Win + R → type %appdata%\Microsoft\Teams → delete the Cache folder
Restart Teams
articles.text: Microsoft Teams Teams Not Loading / Stuck on Loading Screen Close Teams completely from Task Manager Press Win + R → type %appdata%\Microsoft\Teams → delete the Cache folder Restart Teams

articles.title: Teams Calls Dropping or Poor Audio
steps: Check internet — minimum 2 Mbps required for Teams calls
Close other bandwidth-heavy applications
Teams → Settings → Devices → check correct microphone and speaker selected
Try Teams on browser at teams.microsoft.com as a test
articles.text: Microsoft Teams Teams Calls Dropping or Poor Audio Check internet — minimum 2 Mbps required for Teams calls Close other bandwidth-heavy applications Teams → Settings → Devices → check correct microphone and speaker selected Try Teams on browser at teams.microsoft.com as a test

articles.title: Cannot Join a Teams Meeting
steps: Check if meeting link has expired
Try joining from browser instead of app
Clear Teams cache (see steps above)
articles.text: Microsoft Teams Cannot Join a Teams Meeting Check if meeting link has expired Try joining from browser instead of app Clear Teams cache (see steps above)

articles.title: Teams Status Stuck on Away or Offline
steps: Click profile picture → set status manually to Available
Settings → Privacy → toggle Read receipts off and on
Sign out and sign back in
articles.text: Microsoft Teams Teams Status Stuck on Away or Offline Click profile picture → set status manually to Available Settings → Privacy → toggle Read receipts off and on Sign out and sign back in

articles.title: VPN Not Connecting
steps: Check internet connection works without VPN first
Close VPN client completely and reopen
Try disconnecting and reconnecting
Restart the device and try again
Check if VPN credentials expired — reset password if needed
articles.text: VPN VPN Not Connecting Check internet connection works without VPN first Close VPN client completely and reopen Try disconnecting and reconnecting Restart the device and try again Check if VPN credentials expired — reset password if needed

articles.title: VPN Connects but Cannot Access Internal Resources
steps: Disconnect and reconnect VPN
Clear DNS cache → open Command Prompt → type ipconfig /flushdns
Try accessing resource by IP instead of hostname
articles.text: VPN VPN Connects but Cannot Access Internal Resources Disconnect and reconnect VPN Clear DNS cache → open Command Prompt → type ipconfig /flushdns Try accessing resource by IP instead of hostname

articles.title: VPN Disconnects Frequently
steps: Check internet stability — run speedtest.net
Change VPN server if multiple options available
Disable battery saver mode — it can interrupt VPN
If on WiFi — try switching to ethernet
articles.text: VPN VPN Disconnects Frequently Check internet stability — run speedtest.net Change VPN server if multiple options available Disable battery saver mode — it can interrupt VPN If on WiFi — try switching to ethernet

articles.title: No Internet Access in Office
steps: Check if ethernet cable is properly plugged in
Try a different ethernet port on the desk
Restart the device
Check if colleagues in same area have internet — if yes, isolated issue
articles.text: Internet & Network No Internet Access in Office Check if ethernet cable is properly plugged in Try a different ethernet port on the desk Restart the device Check if colleagues in same area have internet — if yes, isolated issue

articles.title: Slow Internet in Office
steps: Close unused browser tabs and applications
Disconnect from VPN temporarily to test speed
Run speedtest.net — expected minimum 50 Mbps on office network
articles.text: Internet & Network Slow Internet in Office Close unused browser tabs and applications Disconnect from VPN temporarily to test speed Run speedtest.net — expected minimum 50 Mbps on office network

articles.title: WiFi Not Showing Nomura Network
steps: Turn WiFi off and on again
Forget the Nomura network and reconnect
Check if device is on approved device list — unregistered devices cannot connect
articles.text: Internet & Network WiFi Not Showing Nomura Network Turn WiFi off and on again Forget the Nomura network and reconnect Check if device is on approved device list — unregistered devices cannot connect

articles.title: Cannot Access Specific Website or Internal Portal
steps: Check if site is blocked by Nomura firewall — some sites are restricted by policy
Try on a different browser
Clear browser cache → Ctrl + Shift + Delete → clear all
If internal portal → check if VPN is connected

escalation.when: Still blocked and should be accessible

articles.text: Internet & Network Cannot Access Specific Website or Internal Portal Check if site is blocked by Nomura firewall — some sites are restricted by policy Try on a different browser Clear browser cache → Ctrl + Shift + Delete → clear all If internal portal → check if VPN is connected

articles.title: Laptop Running Slow
steps: Restart the laptop — do not just close the lid
Close unused applications and browser tabs
Check Task Manager → Ctrl + Shift + Esc → look for high CPU or memory usage
If one application using high CPU → force close it
Check if Windows Update is running in background — let it complete
articles.text: Laptop & Hardware Laptop Running Slow Restart the laptop — do not just close the lid Close unused applications and browser tabs Check Task Manager → Ctrl + Shift + Esc → look for high CPU or memory usage If one application using high CPU → force close it Check if Windows Update is running in background — let it complete

articles.title: Laptop Screen Flickering
steps: Right click Desktop → Display Settings → change refresh rate to 60Hz
Update display driver → Device Manager → Display Adapters → Update Driver
Try connecting external monitor to isolate issue
articles.text: Laptop & Hardware Laptop Screen Flickering Right click Desktop → Display Settings → change refresh rate to 60Hz Update display driver → Device Manager → Display Adapters → Update Driver Try connecting external monitor to isolate issue

articles.title: Laptop Not Charging
steps: Check if power cable is properly connected at both ends
Try a different power outlet
Remove and reinsert the battery if removable
notes: Do not raise P3 for this — raise P2 immediately as employee cannot work if battery dies
articles.text: Laptop & Hardware Laptop Not Charging Check if power cable is properly connected at both ends Try a different power outlet Remove and reinsert the battery if removable Do not raise P3 for this — raise P2 immediately as employee cannot work if battery dies

articles.title: External Monitor Not Detected
steps: Check cable connection at both ends
Try a different cable or port
Right click Desktop → Display Settings → Detect
Press Win + P → select Extend or Duplicate
articles.text: Laptop & Hardware External Monitor Not Detected Check cable connection at both ends Try a different cable or port Right click Desktop → Display Settings → Detect Press Win + P → select Extend or Duplicate

articles.title: Keyboard or Mouse Not Working
steps: Check USB connection — try a different USB port
For wireless — replace batteries or recharge
Restart the device
Try the device on another computer to confirm if hardware fault
articles.text: Laptop & Hardware Keyboard or Mouse Not Working Check USB connection — try a different USB port For wireless — replace batteries or recharge Restart the device Try the device on another computer to confirm if hardware fault

articles.title: Cannot Access a Shared Drive or Folder
steps: Check if you are connected to VPN — required for shared drives
Try accessing by full UNC path e.g. \\servername\foldername
Check with your manager if you should have access
articles.text: Access & Permissions Cannot Access a Shared Drive or Folder Check if you are connected to VPN — required for shared drives Try accessing by full UNC path e.g. \\servername\foldername Check with your manager if you should have access

articles.title: Cannot Access an Internal Application
steps: Check if VPN is connected
Try clearing browser cache and cookies
Try a different browser
Check if your account has the required role or license

escalation.when: Access needed and confirmed by manager

articles.text: Access & Permissions Cannot Access an Internal Application Check if VPN is connected Try clearing browser cache and cookies Try a different browser Check if your account has the required role or license

articles.title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Not Working
steps: Check if authenticator app is showing correct time — time sync issues cause MFA failures
Try the Nomura authenticator app → Refresh codes
Use backup codes if available
If phone number changed → cannot self-serve — must escalate
articles.text: Access & Permissions Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Not Working Check if authenticator app is showing correct time — time sync issues cause MFA failures Try the Nomura authenticator app → Refresh codes Use backup codes if available If phone number changed → cannot self-serve — must escalate

articles.title: Cannot Print — Printer Offline
steps: Check if printer is powered on and connected to network
On laptop → Settings → Printers and Scanners → select printer → Open Queue → clear all jobs
Right click printer → See What's Printing → Printer → uncheck Use Printer Offline
Restart the print spooler → press Win + R → type services.msc → find Print Spooler → Restart
articles.text: Printers Cannot Print — Printer Offline Check if printer is powered on and connected to network On laptop → Settings → Printers and Scanners → select printer → Open Queue → clear all jobs Right click printer → See What's Printing → Printer → uncheck Use Printer Offline Restart the print spooler → press Win + R → type services.msc → find Print Spooler → Restart

articles.title: Print Jobs Stuck in Queue
steps: Open print queue → cancel all pending jobs
Restart Print Spooler service (see above)
Delete files in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS
Restart printer and try again
articles.text: Printers Print Jobs Stuck in Queue Open print queue → cancel all pending jobs Restart Print Spooler service (see above) Delete files in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS Restart printer and try again

articles.title: Reset your Nomura password
steps: Open the Nomura self-service password portal and choose Forgot password.
Confirm your identity with the authenticator app or a code sent to your registered mobile number.
Choose a new password that meets policy: at least 12 characters with upper and lower case, a number and a symbol, and not one you have used before.
Sign out of Outlook, Teams and the VPN client, then sign back in with the new password so saved credentials update.
notes: The service desk will never ask you for your password or a verification code.
If you are off the network you must be connected to the VPN before the new password applies to your laptop.

escalation.when: Self-service reset fails or the portal is unavailable

articles.text: Password & Account Reset your Nomura password password reset forgot change credentials sign login Open the Nomura self-service password portal and choose Forgot password. Confirm your identity with the authenticator app or a code sent to your registered mobile number. Choose a new password that meets policy: at least 12 characters with upper and lower case, a number and a symbol, and not one you have used before. Sign out of Outlook, Teams and the VPN client, then sign back in with the new password so saved credentials update. The service desk will never ask you for your password or a verification code. If you are off the network you must be connected to the VPN before the new password applies to your laptop.

articles.title: Account locked after too many failed sign-ins
steps: Wait 15 minutes. Accounts unlock on their own once the lockout period passes.
Find anything still trying the old password - a phone mail app, a mapped drive, a second laptop - and sign out there first, or it will lock the account again.
Once the lockout clears, sign in again with your current password.
If you no longer know the password, reset it through the self-service portal instead.
notes: Repeated lockouts within an hour almost always mean a device is still caching the old password.

escalation.when: Still locked out after the wait and a password reset

articles.title: Password expiring soon
steps: Change it before it expires rather than after - an expired password locks you out of Outlook and Teams until it is reset.
On the Nomura network or connected to the VPN, press Ctrl + Alt + Delete and choose Change a password.
Enter your current password, then the new one twice.
Sign out and back in so Outlook, Teams and the VPN client pick up the change.
notes: If it has already expired, use the self-service password portal to reset it instead.

escalation.when: Change a password is greyed out or rejects the new password

articles.title: Install approved software on your laptop
steps: Check the software you need is on the approved list below. Only approved software can be installed.
Tell the service desk which title and version you need - several products are available in more than one version.
The service desk triggers the installation remotely. It takes about 15 minutes.
Keep the laptop switched on and connected to the Nomura network until it finishes.

steps: Check the approved list first - the title may be there under a different name or version.
If it is genuinely not listed, it cannot be installed without approval.
Raise a request so a specialist can review whether it can be approved for your role.

articles.title: Ticket priority levels and response times
steps: P1 - Employee completely cannot work - SLA 1 hour
P2 - Major disruption, partially working - SLA 4 hours
P3 - Minor issue, workaround available - SLA next business day
articles.text: Ticket Priority & SLA Ticket priority levels and response times P1 - Employee completely cannot work - SLA 1 hour P2 - Major disruption, partially working - SLA 4 hours P3 - Minor issue, workaround available - SLA next business day

articles.title: Which team handles which issue
steps: Email, Outlook, Teams, Slack - Messaging Team
VPN, WiFi, Internet, Network - Network Team
Laptop, Printer, Monitor, Hardware - End User Computing
Access, Permissions, MFA, Accounts - Identity and Access Management
Unknown or general IT issues - IT Service Desk
articles.text: Ticket Priority & SLA Which team handles which issue Email, Outlook, Teams, Slack - Messaging Team VPN, WiFi, Internet, Network - Network Team Laptop, Printer, Monitor, Hardware - End User Computing Access, Permissions, MFA, Accounts - Identity and Access Management Unknown or general IT issues - IT Service Desk
